title: Tenant-aware audit ingest throttling and compact indexing strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Audit event volume has grown 3x year-over-year. Uncontrolled spikes from automated tenants and bulk RBAC change events are driving storage and query costs and causing ingest backpressure in the hot path. We need a tenant-aware ingest and storage strategy that enforces fair-shares, reduces hot-index cardinality, and enables aggressive compacting without losing regulatory fidelity.

Goal: Implement tenant-aware throttling + adaptive TTL + compact sparse-index format for audit traces so that: (1) peak ingest is smoothed, (2) cold/rare fields are moved to coldstore or off-indexed, (3) common audit queries remain fast, and (4) overall storage spend reduces by at least 40% on burst scenarios while preserving retention guarantees for compliance-tier tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant ingest throttles that can be configured via Console with soft/hard limits and exponential backoff behavior
Adaptive TTL policy engine that assigns hot/standard/cold retention tiers based on tenant SLA and event semantics
New compact sparse-index format for audit events that reduces per-event index size for high-cardinality fields by >=50%
No loss of events for regulated (compliance-tier) tenants: events are ingested deterministically to coldstore with immutable retention metadata
Dashboard + alerting: percent reduction in hotstore tokens and end-to-end ingest latency SLOs verified under synthetic burst tests
Integration tests and a staged rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback hooks
technical_notes: Introduce a token-bucket based per-tenant rate limiter at the edge ingestion layer (ingest-proxy) to enforce fair-share during spikes
Add tenant tags to stream metadata so downstream indexer and tiering controllers can make policy decisions without extra lookups
Implement sparse-index encoding: separate hot-key fields (actor_id, resource_id, action, timestamp) into primary index; store remaining payload as compressed cold blob referenced by event_id
Design compact index mapping to be backwards-compatible with current query layer via a translation shim in the query service
Adaptive TTL engine uses sliding-window heuristics (30/90/365 days) plus manual overrides per tenant; TTL decisions emit audit events for traceability
Coldstore move is append-only and verifies checksum before tombstoning hot-index entries to allow regulatory recoveries
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype token-bucket limiter in dev environment; add tenant tag propagation to ingestion schema (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12298)
Week 2: Build sparse-index writer and cold-blob format; bench write and read latencies on staging cluster (artifact: docs/compact-index-bench-2025-02.pdf)
Week 3: Implement TTL engine and policy surface in Console; add feature flag for canary rollout
Week 4: Run synthetic burst tests (10x normal) with 5 tenants including one compliance-tier; measure cost and latency impact
Week 5: Iterate on query shim for compatibility, add automated recovery playbook, and prepare runbook for SRE
Week 6: Canary rollout to 10% of customers, observe metrics for 72 hours, then escalate to 25% pending success
milestones: P0 prototype token-bucket limiter merged (PR closed): 2025-02-06
Sparse-index v1 commit and benchmarks published: 2025-02-14
Console TTL UI MVP merged behind flag: 2025-02-21
Synthetic burst test report and cost delta: 2025-02-28
risks: Query compatibility regressions: some ad-hoc queries may assume full event JSON in index; mitigated by query shim and opt-in flag
Throttling false positives: aggressive limits could impact customers during legitimate bulk operations; mitigated with soft/hard limit model and request-level whitelisting for admin flows
Complexity of recoveries: moving events to coldstore requires robust verification and rehydration tooling; mitigated by append-only transfer and checksum verification
SLA concerns for high-security tenants: must ensure compliance-tier tenants are never throttled or moved without explicit policy settings
comments: 2025-01-30 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis attached. Observed 3x increase caused by automation bots performing bulk RBAC grants at month boundary. Narrowing approach to tenant-aware limits rather than global ingestion throttles.
2025-02-04 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype limiter implemented; saw 60% reduction in tail latency under synthetic bursts. Need to refine backoff to support batched admin operations.
2025-02-12 - Review (PM - Sofia Morales): PM review requested more visibility per-tenant for cost attribution; added Console surface to ACs.
2025-02-20 - Design (Denise Wu): Reviewed sparse-index format; suggested keeping event schema version on every record to simplify future migrations.
2025-02-25 - Security (Ravi Menon): Security review requested for coldstore encryption and access controls. Action: add KMS key rotation verification to runbook.
2025-03-03 - SRE (Marta Ivanova): Load test passing; added automated rollback job to abort compaction if error rate > 0.25% over 5m window. Preparing canary config.
